the expression of the HSP and MPR proteins in the colon cancer cells is increased by rhTGFβ1, and that this is associated with a decreased expression of the cytokine IL6.

rhTGFβ1 and/or camptothecins may be able to modulate the expression of Hsps and MRP in tumours, thus influencing tumour progression, and may also modulate the release of soluble mediators of tumour progression, thus limiting their effects on tumour growth.

the use of rhTGF-ß1 and/or CFT-11 in cancer treatment should be carefully evaluated in order to avoid the induction of resistance mechanisms and to limit the side effects of these agents on tumour cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of Hsp27, Hsp72, and MRP in colon tumour cells is influenced by the presence of normal cells and by rhTGF-beta1 and/or Cpt-11.
the use of CPT-11 and rhTGF-ß1 in the treatment of colon carcinoma should be carefully evaluated in order to prevent or limit the emergence of resistance to chemotherapy and tumour progression.
the combination of rhTGF- β1 and CPT-11 can be used to increase the efficacy of chemotherapy in colon cancer patients.
